Commentary.Commentary: We are back with the chase. The umpires have made their way to the middle followed by the players of South Africa. Steven Taylor and Andries Gous are the openers for USA. For South Africa, Marco Jansen will bowl the first over.
... The Run Chase ...

The bowling from USA was not up to the mark as they leaked runs on both sides and did not stick to their plans but eventually, they will feel they have kept the opposition about 15 runs or so short of what could have been an even higher total. The bowlers lacked discipline and gave a lot of 'hit-me' deliveries. Harmeet Singh got a timely double strike in his last over. Saurabh Netravalkar was once again spot on and bowled tremendously having figures of 21 for 2. The target is a big one but we have seen USA has got the players to chase this down. Can they do it against a quality bowling unit of South Africa? We shall find that out soon as the chase is up next.

Skipper of South Africa, Aiden Markram is up for a chat and he says they’re happy with the total. Adds the conditions got better after 5-6 overs and it got difficult for the bowlers after that. Mentions that he is happy with the contribution from the top order and feels this is nicely set up for them. Reckons that the surface doesn’t look to favor the spinners yet but they have got quality spinners and he is counting on them to do well and get the job done.

A brilliant knock with the bat from Quinton de Kock and co, helps South Africa put up a show with the bat as they score 194 after 20 overs which is also the highest-ever Men's T20I total at this ground. After being asked to bat first, the Proteas started on the front foot and came out with a positive intent. Quinton de Kock in particular was the aggressor and smashed the bowlers of USA all around the park. He went on to play a superb knock of 74 off just 40 deliveries. It was another meager out for Reeza Hendricks but de Kock was well helped by Aiden Markramas he played the perfect anchor, allowing de Kock to keep going big. Aiden Markram fell short of a deserving half-century and was caught by Ali Khan when he was on 46.  Heinrich Klaasen ended the innings with a good hand of 36 runs as Tristan Stubbs also mustered up a few crucial runs.

FOUR! Glorious shot from Tristan Stubbs to end the innings! Ali Khan bowls it a bit full and at the stumps, Stubbs switches his position and plays the reverse scoop right back over the keeper's head with good timing and the ball goes into the ropes. South Africa finish with a huge total of 194/4 on the board!

Commentary.Commentary: Done and dusted with the pre-match formalities and it is now time to get the Super Eight stage underway! The umpires are out in the middle and so are the players of USA who take their places on the field. It will be the pairing of Quinton de Kock and Reeza Hendricks that will open the innings for South Africa. The in-form Saurabh Netravalkar has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Just the one slip in place. Let's go...

It is time for the pre-match formalities. Sir Curtly Ambrose brings out that coveted Trophy and places it on the podium. Players from both sides have lined up for their national anthems. It will be the national anthem of South Africa followed by that of USA.

The skipper of South Africa, Aiden Markram says this looks like a good pitch and they weren’t sure what to do had they won the toss so they are not too bothered by it. Informs that they have gone with an extra-spinner hence Keshav Maharaj gets into the XI and replaces Ottneil Baartman. Mentions that the change is purely because of the condition and Ottneil Baartman is unlucky to miss out today.

Aaron Jones, the stand-in skipper of USA says that they will bowl first. Reckons it will be a good wicket and if anything, the seamers will get the most out of it right at the start. Informs that they are going in with the extra spinner. Adds that the wicket seems similar to Dallas and it will play well and will look to bowl well upfront. Monank Patel is still missing out due to a shoulder injury.

South Africa (Playing XI) - Quinton de Kock (WK), Reeza Hendricks, Aiden Markram (C), Heinrich Klaasen, David Miller, Tristan Stubbs, Marco Jansen, Keshav Maharaj (replaces Ottneil Baartman), Kagiso Rabada, Anrich Nortje, Tabraiz Shamsi.

USA (Playing XI) - Steven Taylor, Shayan Jahangir, Andries Gous (WK), Aaron Jones (C), Nitish Kumar, Corey Anderson, Harmeet Singh, Jessy Singh, Nosthush Kenjige (replaces Shadley van Schalkwyk), Ali Khan, Saurabh Netravalkar.
TOSS - The stand-in skipper of USA, Aaron Jones has won the coin flip and he informs that they will BOWL first.

South Africa on the other hand have arrived in the Super 8 with a 100 percent win record. They set the tone right from the get-go as they demolished Sri Lanka to start their campaign. The side then defeated the other three sides in their group but none of those victories were convincing. The batters have had a torrid time playing in the States and failed to adjust to the conditions in the Windies in their last game but they would be delighted to move to the Windies for the remaining games. The bowling has looked superb for them with Anrich Nortje gaining some form while others doing the clean-up around him but it is the batting that needs to step up and take some responsibility now. The likes of Quinton de Kock, Aiden Markram, Heinrich Klaasen and Reeza Hendricks have yet to score something significant while the form of David Miller and Tristan Stubbs, in particular, has been a positive for them. The Proteas would be aiming for a perfect start to the Super 8s while USA would be eyeing another upset in the tournament. Stay tuned for toss and team updates…

It’s been a fabulous past couple of months for USA in the history of cricket as they won a bilateral series against Bangladesh in preparation for this World Cup and when the time arrived they defeated Canada and Pakistan to advance to the Super 8. They had a fair bit of luck their way as well with them earning a crucial point against Ireland in their last group-stage game. The side has showcased its gritty nature and has won those crunch moments in their first two games. Skipper Monank Patel has led the side brilliantly and has impressed all with the way he has marshaled his troops. Steven Taylor, Andries Gous, Aaron Jones and Nitish Kumar have batted well while Corey Anderson and Harmeet Singh are yet to shine as finishers. One of the stories of this World Cup has been the way Saurabh Netravalkar has performed and scalped the big fishes throughout the tournament so far. Ali Khan, Nosthush Kenjige and Jessy Singh have given Saurabh Netravalkar the much-needed support from the other end. The team looks balanced and they would be itching to rub shoulders against the Proteas.

Hello and welcome to all our esteemed viewers. The group stages are done and now we are left with 8 teams in 2 groups of 4 each. The first game of the Super 8 will be played between the co-hosts USA and South Africa. Sir Vivian Richards Stadium, North Sound, Antigua will host this mouth-watering encounter.
... MATCHDAY ...

The cricketing world is all pumped up as the Super 8 stage of the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2024 has finally arrived. After an enthralling league phase that witnessed some scintillating performances and nail-biting finishes, eight titans of the game now stand tall, poised to engage in an epic battle for supremacy. For the first time in this prestigious tournament's 17-year history, a record-breaking 20 nations graced the global stage, each fueled by dreams of cricketing glory. The ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2024 has been a stage for the underdogs to shine, as the associate nations have fought remarkably against the cricketing giants. Match 1 of the Super 8s features the dangerous South African side going up against the emerging stars of the USA. Sir Vivian Richards Stadium of North Sound, Antigua will play host to this exciting clash. The co-hosts, USA, have enjoyed a dream run so far, surpassing expectations with their impressive performances. However, their challenge has now further elevated as the competition intensifies, and the diversity of opponents escalates in this critical phase. Their journey began with a resounding triumph over their northern neighbors, Canada, but the real blockbuster moment came when they outclassed and outfoxed the tournament's runner-up, Pakistan, in a Super Over thriller that had the cricketing world on the edge of their seats. That victory was a true announcement of their arrival on the global cricketing landscape. Despite a setback against the formidable Indian side, the USA's resilience and fighting spirit were undeniable. Saurabh Netravalkar has been the standout performer with the ball, gaining all the praise and attention from across the cricketing world for his skillful bowling, while he has been complemented pretty well by his fellow pacers, Ali Khan and Jessy Singh. The spin duo of Nosthush Kenjige and Harmeet Singh have also played their part, being decently economical and providing valuable support to the pace attack. Aaron Jones has shouldered the bulk of the responsibility with the bat, displaying immaculate resistance and doing the heavy lifting with his resolute knocks. Complementing him have been the dynamic skipper Monank Patel and Steven Taylor, who have provided steady starts on the tricky and slow tracks. Andries Gous and Nitish Kumar have further bolstered the middle order and then there’s Corey Anderson who boasts the ability to play those crucial clutch knocks in the backend coupled with bowling crucial overs. Overall, their batting unit has looked impressive and it would interesting to see how they resist against the formidable Proteas pace quartet that has been consistent so far. Anrich Nortje has regained his form and is literally darting thunderbolts and taking crucial wickets. The others, Kagiso Rabada, Marco Jansen, and Ottneil Baartman have given no respite for the batters either. While their spin attack has floated between crafty Keshav Maharaj and Tabraiz Shamsi, no one can deny the havoc they can wreak, especially on spin-friendly tracks of the Caribbean. South Africa's batting order has been a cause for concern. The form of their skipper, Aiden Markram, has been a worrying factor. Additionally, the usually reliable opening duo of Quinton de Kock and Reeza Hendricks have been in sort of a lean patch, leaving the team's batting unit searching for consistent contributions. In the midst of this, the silver lining has been David Miller and Heinrich Klaasen, who have emerged as the saviors, shouldering the responsibility of rescuing them time and again with their gritty, resolute knocks. However, once this batting unit finds its rhythm, there’s no stopping it as these blokes can go all guns blazing, to their reputation. While Antigua too, hasn't been friendly for the batters, as evident with the low-scoring encounters of the group phase, it’s a battle against the South African pace battery versus the in-form batting unit of the USA. Who do you think will win?
